title: Jacobi-Zariski sequence of a tower of fields is exact on the left
statement: Let $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ be field extensions. For a ring map $R\to S$ let $H_1(L_{S/R})$ be the first homology of the naive cotangent complex $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}$ of the canonical presentation $R[S]\to S$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and $\Omega_{S/R}$ the module of K\"ahler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Let $a:H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM\to H_1(L_{M/K})$ be the $M$-linear map $h\otimes c\mapsto c\cdot\iota_*(h)$, where $\iota_*:H_1(L_{L/K})\to H_1(L_{M/K})$ is induced by the morphism of presentations $K[L]\to K[M]$, $[l]\mapsto[l]$, over the square $K=K$, $L\subseteq M$ [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentation-h1-functoriality]. Then the sequence of $M$-vector spaces $$0\to H_1(L_{L/K})\otimes_LM\xrightarrow{a}H_1(L_{M/K})\xrightarrow{v}H_1(L_{M/L})\xrightarrow{\partial}\Omega_{L/K}\otimes_LM\xrightarrow{w}\Omega_{M/K}\xrightarrow{z}\Omega_{M/L}\to0,$$ with $v,\partial,w,z$ the maps of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for $K\to L\to M$ [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-homology-sequence], is exact. In particular $a$ is injective.

proof.text: Prove left_injective_at_regular_stage. Apply jacobiZariski_left_injective_of_regularSequence at a regular presentation of C over L, obtaining the injective map j from the kernel of the base-changed cotangent differential. Define t on C tensor H1(K,L) by tensoring the inclusion H1(K,L) into the canonical conormal module; its image lies in the differential kernel, as checked by tensor induction. Since C is flat over the field L, Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap makes t injective. Apply the ambient conormal formula specifying j. Tensor induction identifies j composed with t with (H1Cotangent.map K K L C).liftBaseChange C. Thus the canonical left map is injective at every regular stage. No Tor vanishing/comparison theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 07D4 regular-sequence clause; Tag 07E2 via Tag 07D5

proof.text: Prove tensor_conormal_finite_support by tensor induction. A pure tensor m tensor h, with h represented by a polynomial g in the canonical presentation ideal I(L/K), maps to the conormal class of [m] times rename(algebraMap L M)(g); canonical_conormal_tmul proves this using the presentation map on generators and linearity of the ideal quotient. The finite set for a pure tensor is {m}. In every L-subalgebra S containing m, use the same polynomial formula with m regarded as an element of S. Variable renaming sends that representative to the one over M. For zero take the zero polynomial and empty set; for a sum add representatives and take the union of the finite sets. This produces a representative G for the conormal image of x and a finite E such that every S containing E has a tensor y mapping to x and a polynomial q representing the conormal image of y, with rename(q)=G.

source.place: Tag 07E2 via Tag 07D5 and Algebra Tag 07BQ: finite-support argument for canonical presentations, written out in Lean

proof.text: Prove relation_square_finite_support by induction on membership in I(M/K) times I(M/K). For a product p*q of relations take the union of their finite variable sets. In a subalgebra containing those variables, MvPolynomial.exists_rename_eq_of_vars_subset_range gives lifts p′,q′. Evaluation commutes with renaming (eval_rename_subalgebra), and the inclusion S -> M is injective, so the lifts evaluate to zero and lie in I(S/K). Their product belongs to I(S/K)^2 and renames to p*q. For a sum use the union of the finite sets and add the lifted square-members. Consequently any polynomial G in I(M/K)^2 has a finite variable set F ensuring that G lifts to I(S/K)^2 in every subalgebra containing F.

source.place: Tag 07E2 via Tag 07D5 and Algebra Tag 07BQ: descent of the relation ideal and its square

proof.text: For x in the kernel of the canonical left map, step 3 gives G and E. Its conormal class is zero, so Extension.Cotangent.mk_eq_zero_iff places G in I(M/K)^2. Step 4 gives F. Apply FieldTheory.exists_completeIntersection_subalgebra L M to E union F, obtaining an injective map iota from a regular polynomial quotient into M. Set S=iota.range. The quotient map followed by iota.rangeRestrict is surjective onto S and has kernel exactly the regular-sequence ideal, since iota is injective. Step 3 gives y and q at S; step 4 gives r in I(S/K)^2 with the same image G. Injectivity of variable renaming implies q=r, so the conormal image and hence the H1 image of y is zero. Step 2 makes y zero; its image x is zero. LinearMap.ker_eq_bot gives injectivity. Combine with step 1 to obtain the unchanged statement.

Statement unchanged. New nodes: 07BV (unsplit), 07D4 regular-sequence case (unsplit).
